messages:
carol: Heads-up: CI changes tomorrow will push SAST reports to a new bucket encrypted with customer-managed KMS. Anyone know if the security team can still download raw SARIF? Need to confirm audit logs.
ben: cc @eng-platform @eng-infra — what's the intended RBAC for the new bucket? Security currently reads SARIF for triage.
erin: We planned to add a role 'scanner.reader' with permission 'scan:read_reports'. That role maps to group security-scanners. Will that allow downloads of artifacts or just list/get metadata?
dave: Download will be allowed if we use object-level ACLs, but prefer to avoid ACLs. Alternative: expose a short-lived signed URL service from infra so we avoid ACLs entirely.
frank: KMS note: rotating the CMK will rewrap objects; S3 re-encrypts but services need kms:Decrypt for access during rewrap. If a customer uses their own KMS, we need cross-account grants or use proxy rewrap. Also watch for kms:GenerateDataKey usage in upload flow.
carol: Important for triage: if we lose raw SARIF access in bulk, we lose stack traces and file context. We currently use `codeql` region details to map owners. Need to ensure triage tools still work.
ben: Proposal: keep read for security-scanners, mark downloads as audit-only and log every GET to central immutable audit-lake. Consider requiring an approval step (or 2FA) before issuing a signed URL.
erin: 2FA for service accounts is painful. Instead: approval workflow in Console -> approver clicks to issue temp token (30m) scoped to download. That gives an auditable event and avoids ACLs.
devsec-bot: New finding: SAST job 2345 produced 17 high-confidence potential secrets (mostly env placeholders) — flagged to #eng-security. Results: https://ci.company/sast/2345 (raw SARIF available if permitted).
carol: Those look like noise. We need suppression metadata so triagers can mark false positives with reason and confidence. Also can we attach suppressed=true to SARIF results so audits show suppression intent?
dave: SARIF supports additionalProperties and result.properties. We can add 'redwood:suppressed' and 'redwood:suppression_reason'. Changing format is fine but must remain backward compatible with our triage UI (fallback to old keys).
erin: Also DAST pipeline note: dynamic scans produce HARs/recordings that sometimes include PII (cookies, auth headers). Ensure client-side redaction before upload, plus KMS encryption in transit. Recommend stripping Set-Cookie, Authorization headers, and masking values in bodies.
frank: Action items summary: 1) eng-infra to propose RBAC policy mapping scanner.reader -> security-scanners and document constraints. 2) eng-platform to design ephemeral signed-download service (30m tokens, audit events). 3) devsec to add suppression schema to SARIF and provide migration plan for triage UI. 4) security to draft audit policy for download events + cross-KMS grant guidance. I'll own the cross-KMS grant PR.
ben: I'll open the IAM PR for the scanner role + policy today: https://git.company/infra/scan-rbac/pull/12 :thumbsup:
erin: If anyone's triaging tomorrow, tag me. Also please add a short runbook to /runbooks/sast-dast-access.md describing the approval flow and audit checks.
carol: Thanks all — tagging @security-oncall for visibility. If there are blockers we'll sync 9:30am tomorrow.
